reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared features across instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both pattern recognition and statistical validation of feature influence, especially for features that may appear common but are not semantically meaningful. The combination increases confidence in identifying truly spurious, shared features driving misclassification.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 9686) and list their values.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features across all three instances with their corresponding values

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, relationship=Husband) is semantically related to income class (>50K), or if it is a spurious correlate that may be driving misclassification.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A judgment on whether the shared feature is semantically relevant or spurious

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides robust, game-theoretic feature importance scores that can reveal which features have high attribution despite lacking semantic relevance. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability and gradient-based attribution, helping validate whether the shared feature drives predictions. Sensitivity analysis confirms the feature's impact by ablation, ensuring it is not just correlated but causally influential. Together, these tools validate spurious patterns across instances.
